text:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV_CACHE_EVICTION_RATE_HIGH fired for service=runtime-gpu-pool region=us-west-2 (severity=page)

alex: paging oncall — eviction rate spiked to ~45% over last 5m. seeing increased forward latency and >250 error traces. paging priority: P1?

maria: oncall here, grabbing it. confirming impact to customers (any 5xx spike on public endpoints?)

oliver: frontend svc 503s up ~3x in the last 10m, correlated with RETRY storms. root cause likely cache misses causing more compute/memory thrash.

sam: what triggered the alert? threshold was 20% eviction rate, 5m. seems noisy but this is sustained.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0423. Incident channel #incident-1708200000-evictions auto-created. PagerDuty: rota=oncall-rotation, escalation=30m.

oncall-rotation: acked. handoff note: i'll stay until stabilization or 21:30 PT.

maria: quick triage: checked KV cache metrics — hit_rate dropped from 88% -> 52% around 1708199400. eviction_rate rose from 8% -> 46%. memory pressure on nodes increased.

emily: adding that customer impact: a few enterprise customers reported increased latency/timeouts on batch embeddings. CS ticket #CS-918 flagged.

alex: mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily raise cache size (if infra allows) 2) add routing fallback to smaller model to reduce pressure 3) throttle non-critical background jobs. Which is fastest?

oliver: fastest is throttling background batch jobs — can flip a flag in jobqueue to pause non-real-time batches. I can push that now.

sam: I can patch alert to reduce noise after we stabilize, but first we need to avoid cascading failures.

maria: doing controlled pause of batch jobs now.

maria: paused jobs -> 1708200300. observing metrics...

alex: monitoring logs and latency dashboards. eviction_rate trending down to 22% at 1708200600. hit_rate up to 74%. errors falling.

incident-bot: NOTE: auto-suggested runbook step applied: paused low-priority batch jobs (runbook step 3).

emily: CS update: informed affected customers of mitigation and ETA for postmortem. they're still seeing some retries but getting fewer.

oliver: follow-up actions we should take (summary): - tune eviction alert to reduce noise - add dedicated cache hit-rate panel to per-service dashboard - create eviction-rate burn-down grafana alert - add runbook section for pausing batch jobs and increasing per-pod cache size if allowed

alex: agreed. propose tuning alert from eviction_rate > 20% for 5m to > 30% for 3m AND require sustained drop in hit_rate (combined condition). avoids transient thrash.

maria: also propose a soft-alert (warning) at 20% 5m that goes to MTL channel (not page) so we can eyeball before paging.

sam: I'll draft Prometheus alert rule now. putting snippet here for review:

```
# suggested alert: KV cache eviction noisy -> avoid paging on transients
- alert: KVCacheHighEviction
  expr: |
    (sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (service) / sum(kv_cache_items_total) by (service)) > 0.30
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High KV cache eviction rate ({{ $labels.service }})"

- alert: KVCacheEvictionWarning
  expr: (sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (service) / sum(kv_cache_items_total) by (service)) > 0.20
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warn
```

sam: also adding a compound check with hit_rate: only page if eviction > 30% and hit_rate < 65% for 3m.

alex: add Grafana panels: - per-region hit_rate heatmap - eviction_rate histogram by pod - 5m/1h rolling windows so SREs can quickly spot regressions.

emily: can product/console team add a dashboard tile for customer-visible cache KPIs? PM requested earlier. good time to sync.

oliver: I'll open a small RFC in docs (eng-sre/dashboard-requests) with the panel json and queries, and link it to the sprint ticket.

maria: runbook update (quick paste):
1) If eviction_rate > 30% and hit_rate < 65%: pause low-priority batches -> notify product & CS -> consider increasing cache allocation on pods -> if not improving, scale out cache-capable nodes.
2) If eviction spikes but hit_rate remains >75%: treat as transient, do not page, monitor for 15m.

sre-lead: approving the change to alert thresholds. sam, please submit PR to prometheus-alerts and add unit tests for the rule. alex/oliver, coordinate dashboard PRs. schedule a post-incident review tomorrow.

alex: PRs in flight: prometheus-alerts #432 (draft), grafana-dashboards #210 (panel json), runbooks #87 (runbook update). ETA for all: EOD tomorrow.

emily: CS noted impacted customers were notified. we'll include timeline and mitigation steps in postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> metrics stabilizing. Next step: postmortem and alert tuning.

oncall-rotation: handing off to day oncall at 1708203300. i'll leave a follow-up note in the incident channel.

maria: handing off to emily (day oncall). leaving runbook pointer and current metrics.

emily: taking over. will run through the checklist and own the postmortem. thanks everyone for fast responses. :thumbsup:

sre-lead: good work. action items assigned, let's make the alert less noisy and add the hit-rate panels — aim for more signal, less churn.

alex: closing thread here, moving discussion to #incident-1708200000-evictions for postmortem drafting.
